nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale?
flashcards.back: Amazon SageMaker is the end-to-end managed ML platform on AWS that covers data labeling, training, tuning, deployment, and monitoring. Rekognition, Comprehend and Glue are higher-level or data-prep services.

flashcards.front: Which Amazon service is purpose-built for generative AI applications using foundation models from multiple providers via a single API?
flashcards.back: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that exposes foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Amazon Titan, etc.) through a single serverless API for building generative AI apps.

flashcards.front: A company wants to extract entities, key phrases and sentiment from customer support tickets. Which AWS service is the best fit?
flashcards.back: Amazon Comprehend is the NLP service that detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII in text. Translate handles language translation, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Kendra is enterprise search.

flashcards.front: A team is integrating a large language model into a customer-support assistant. They notice that small changes in how they word the request — adding examples, specifying tone, asking the model to think step by step — dramatically change the output quality without changing model weights. What is the primary purpose of the discipline that systematises these changes?
flashcards.back: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing the text input so that a foundation model produces accurate, on-task responses without modifying the model's weights. Quantization, retraining and encryption are unrelated optimization or security activities.

statements.text: Amazon Bedrock exposes foundation models from multiple providers behind a single API.
statements.explanation: Bedrock is the managed entrypoint for FMs from Anthropic, Amazon, Cohere, Meta, Mistral and others — one API surface.

statements.text: Amazon SageMaker is a generative-AI chat product for end-users.
statements.explanation: SageMaker is the build/train/deploy platform for ML. The end-user chat product is Amazon Q.

statements.text: Amazon Q can be grounded on a company's own data sources.
statements.explanation: Amazon Q connects to enterprise data via connectors so answers are grounded on internal documents, code, and tickets.

statements.text: Foundation models in Bedrock require you to manage the underlying GPU instances yourself.
statements.explanation: Bedrock is fully serverless — the infrastructure is abstracted away. SageMaker is where you'd manage instances if needed.

statements.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique to ground LLM responses in external knowledge at inference time.
statements.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant context from a knowledge base, then injects it into the prompt — no model retraining needed.

statements.text: Prompt engineering is a substitute for fine-tuning whenever the task requires deep domain knowledge the model never saw.
statements.explanation: If the model truly lacks the domain knowledge, prompting alone isn't enough — fine-tuning or RAG is required.

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A team is choosing the right ML paradigm for a fraud-detection problem. They have a large historical dataset where each past transaction is labelled fraud or legitimate by investigators. They want a model that learns to predict the label on new transactions. Which paradigm fits?
flashcards.back: Supervised learning trains a model on input-output pairs (labeled data) to predict labels for new inputs. Unsupervised finds structure in unlabeled data; reinforcement learns by reward signals.

flashcards.front: A model performs extremely well on the training set but poorly on unseen data. What is this called?
flashcards.back: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data including its noise, so it generalizes poorly. Common mitigations: more data, regularization, simpler models, dropout, or early stopping.

flashcards.front: A regulated lender deploys a credit-scoring model and must demonstrate to auditors which features drove each decision and whether the model exhibits bias across demographic groups. AWS markets a service that surfaces feature attributions and bias metrics across the model lifecycle. Which service is it?
flashcards.back: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection on data and models and uses SHAP values for explainability of predictions. Ground Truth handles labeling, Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows, Feature Store stores features.

flashcards.front: A media app needs to convert article text into natural-sounding speech in multiple languages and voices. The team wants a managed AWS service that handles neural text-to-speech without operating their own infrastructure. Which service does this?
flashcards.back: Amazon Polly is the text-to-speech (TTS) service. Transcribe is the reverse (speech-to-text), Translate is for language translation, and Lex is for conversational chatbots.

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.
